The HKMA’s long-term and near-term emissions reduction targets were formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which was also validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has appointed the HKQAA to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper use and waste data disclosed in this report.6 The scope and criteria of verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” section of this report. In addition to publishing its Annual Report 2022, the HKMA published its first standalone Sustainability Report 2022 in 2023. The HKMA’s efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognised with an ESG Award in the Public Sector/Not-for-profit category of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants’ Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023. The HKMA is the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for achieving good ESG standards, presenting a clear and easy-to-read Sustainability Report, and demonstrating its commitment to highly transparent and accountable reporting by appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report. In addition, the HKMA received the highest accolade, the Gold Award in the Non-profit Making and Charitable Organisations category, at the Hong Kong Management Association’s Best Annual Reports Awards 2023. The judging panel commended the HKMA’s annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making effective use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA’s commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its people and the community as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations, and its internal Green Office Guidelines provide staff with guidance on resource use and office waste generation. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When refurbishing offices, existing furniture and fitting materials are reused wherever possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly construction and decorative materials are given priority. The HKMA has consistently adopted this approach, resulting in Gold certifications under LEED7 and BEAM Plus Interiors8 for parts of its offices at Two International Finance Centre refurbished in 2021 and 2022 respectively. Improving energy efficiency through the adoption of new technologies and the effective use of existing technologies remains one of the HKMA’s priorities. In addition to promoting good practices, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to conserve electricity, other energy-saving measures include using light-emitting diode lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimising energy use in information technology network infrastructure. The HKMA’s energy consumption continued to decline, reaching 2.59 megawatt-hours per capita9 in 2023, down 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA’s day-to-day operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly arise from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e per capita,10 down 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software and meeting facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies and automated and streamlined workflows to create a digital workplace and enhance online collaboration within the organisation.11 Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of meeting at the HKMA. To further reduce paper use and improve efficiency, electronic processes are used for most internal administrative matters. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital ways of working by replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. The implementation of an electronic records management system is also under way. These green and digital measures have delivered positive results. The HKMA’s paper-use intensity was 11.55 kilograms per capita in 2023, representing a substantial decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events resumed in-person formats following the COVID-19 pandemic, and given the need to promote the development of Hong Kong as an international financial centre, overseas business travel by relevant HKMA staff was unavoidable. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff attending overseas events to take direct flights or combine different business trips where practicable. At the corporate level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participated in Gold Standard12-certified carbon offsetting projects to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these projects involved waste-to-energy conversion, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA’s procurement process takes sustainability and environmental considerations into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation’s procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised and follows the environmental specifications in the Government’s Green Procurement List, particularly for the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. All suppliers are also required to undertake to comply with environmental regulations. In accordance with the “4R” principles of Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimising waste generation and managing waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. A breakdown of non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, is set out in the “Performance Summary” section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated directly for the first time in the red packet recycling programme organised by the property management company of its offices at International Finance Centre. Staff contributed around 3,000 used but still pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently passed to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use during the Lunar New Year in the following year. As the HKMA’s operational and backup data centres account for a major share of the organisation’s overall energy consumption, both data centres were upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres and achieve optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE).13 In 2023, the HKMA’s two data centres received Gold and Platinum ratings respectively under the BEAM Plus Data Centres Existing assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive these ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centres has long been a priority of the technical team. To this end, the team incorporated green design into the renovation works and adopted good energy-efficient practices to lower PUE and achieve the relevant targets, including round-the-clock monitoring of the environmental facilities at the data centres and continuous enhancements to environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continued to improve energy use at the data centres, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the data centres’ green performance and formulate recommendations for further enhancements in all areas. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after its completion, the HKMA began preparations for obtaining Green Data Centre certification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process was comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team implemented enhancement measures based on the consultant’s recommendations, covering areas from energy performance to health elements in the working environment of the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) 2023 environmental data (“2023 Data”). The 2023 Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, GHG emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, and non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) in 2023, their respective intensities, and changes in these data compared with 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data include the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA’s GHG emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison, except for food waste. The scope of verification covered a total of five office and warehouse assets, comprising four offices located at (1) Two International Finance Centre, (2) Hopewell Centre, (3) One Pacific Place and (4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at (5) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the five assets. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to enable an opinion and conclusion to be reached with a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the data were tested by tracing selected sample data back to their sources. The underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking were also reviewed and tested for reliability. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for collecting and reporting the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency’s verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data are materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed that 2024 was the warmest year on record and the first year in which the global temperature exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions, after moderating slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, have recently reached a new high, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. As efforts to combat global warming continue, climate-related risks are bound to intensify, with unpredictable implications for the economy and financial markets. Moreover, current geopolitical tensions, increasing fragmentation of the global economy, the risk of heightened energy security concerns and economic uncertainty are all making it more challenging for countries to tackle climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Among regions worldwide, Asia faces particularly acute transition challenges. As noted by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only an engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change. Asia therefore plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leadership role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive the region’s transition. To this end, the HKMA published the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainability considerations into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on both enhancing the financial sector’s capacity to address climate-related risks and helping the sector capture emerging opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA’s sustainability work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector in achieving net zero, investing in a sustainable future, financing net zero, and making sustainability more inclusive. The banking system plays a pivotal role in Hong Kong’s and Asia’s net-zero transition, but banks themselves also face considerable risks during the transition. Under the Action Agenda, we have set ambitious targets requiring all banks to strive to achieve net zero in their own operations by 2030 and in their financed emissions by 2050. We also require all banks to enhance their disclosures of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks’ climate risk management, we also provide guidance on transition planning to help them enhance their transition capabilities and better manage the associated risks. We are also undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong’s sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing the transparency of related activities within the industry. In addition, we are refining the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year to include more sustainable activities, including transition activities. By providing clear criteria, we hope to channel more capital towards sustainability- and transition-related projects. Climate change gives rise to significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. At the same time, however, it also presents the Exchange Fund with opportunities for growth and positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainability impacts can complement each other and are not mutually exclusive. In view of this, we are committed to striving to achieve net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s Investment Portfolio by 2050, and have pledged under the Action Agenda to support Asia’s climate transition through the Exchange Fund’s investments. Sustainable investments currently account for more than 10% of the Investment Portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate Asia’s low-carbon economic transition through co-investments. We also published the inaugural “HKMA ESG Expectations” document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to exercise active ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financing is particularly important for accelerating the region’s transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances by Asian issuers, including Mainland provincial and municipal governments, Hong Kong plays an important role in channelling capital to accelerate the region’s transition. The Action Agenda outlines our vision of developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable finance platform in the region, as well as our goal of promoting sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government Sustainable Bond Programme to drive green bond innovation, including the world’s first multi-currency digital bond issuance in February last year, to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to cover transition finance instruments in May last year, and launching the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November last year, we have been committed to encouraging issuers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financial platform to raise the funds needed for their decarbonisation transition. A sound transition requires not only capital and innovation, but also the support of an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent disclosures, and industry talent equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we have committed under the Action Agenda to supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures and bridging the region’s gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge. We have made good progress in supporting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosures, particularly by providing accessible and user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability disclosures by small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched the professional-level “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners to strengthen the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we engaged different sectors of the community in sustainability discussions, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations are aligned with our sustainability vision. Under the Action Agenda, we have pledged to achieve net zero in our own operations by 2030, 20 years earlier than our original commitment. We are also actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the Government. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a selection criterion in our procurement processes. At the same time, we continue to enhance operational efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainability within the organisation, and inspire our staff to participate actively in sustainability efforts. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic geopolitical shifts have added uncertainty to global climate action. Yet climate change is an indisputable fact and is gradually intensifying. In tackling climate change, the current circumstances leave no room for complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong’s financial system while creating opportunities in the process. Moving into 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, spare no effort in advancing our sustainability work, and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges ahead, we will remain steadfast in our commitment to supporting a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing our generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA published the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out the HKMA’s vision in this area, including our future directions, the timelines for achieving various goals, and how we expect the industry to collaborate in taking the relevant work forward. Through strategic policymaking, enhanced supervisory engagement and improvements to internal operations, the HKMA plans to strengthen the capacity of Hong Kong’s financial sector and the HKMA itself to address climate-related risks and support Asia’s transition to a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also seeks to exert influence and contribute to the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking supervisor, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in remaining safe and sound throughout the transition to net zero. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - commencing a new round of thematic examinations and conducting a third round of climate risk management consultations to review banks’ implementation of the HKMA’s relevant supervisory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - finalising the incorporation of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s supervisor-driven stress testing framework; - continuing to advance the incorporation of climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; - commencing preparatory work to develop relevant supervisory requirements for the local implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - completing the development of a new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide banks with guidance on transition planning; and - sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to its role as a banking supervisor, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator to promote the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and support banks in financing the transition. We published Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate the relevant flow of capital. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase 2 of the taxonomy to expand its coverage by incorporating transition elements, adding more green economic activities and introducing climate change adaptation objectives. In addition, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks’ adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the region’s sustainable financing needs. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Sustainable Bond Programme, the expanded scope of which will cover sustainable projects such as social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and set an example for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise sustainable funding. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates from the Mainland and elsewhere to raise green funding in Hong Kong. Meanwhile, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including by providing subsidies through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme to prospective issuers of digital green bonds. Despite growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and corporates, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make such disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a broader range of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can make existing resources more accessible and easier to use; and collaborate with major local industry bodies to provide the training needed by the industry. The sustainable finance market is evolving rapidly, necessitating the expansion of the local talent pool and the closing of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and across the region. The HKMA’s key priorities for 2025 include collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training for the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework, and identifying areas where the industry requires further training through the forthcoming Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026–2030 study. In addition, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to step up the promotion of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme and review the scope of the Scheme. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to introduce dedicated programmes across Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analyses, offering targeted capacity-building and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps for making green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed the Exchange Fund’s Investment Portfolio to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in support of the overall economic transition. Through a pragmatic and robust responsible investment approach, we will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can contribute to positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in corporate sustainability. In line with the accelerated timeline for its net-zero commitment announced in the Action Agenda, the HKMA will continue to advance corporate sustainability by progressively incorporating environmental and social considerations into its strategies, risk assessments and reporting at a pragmatic pace. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. In addition, we will conduct an energy audit and use technological solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government’s publication of the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will remain committed to applying the principles of energy efficiency and conservation in selecting data centres for planned upgrades. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience of our staff, banks and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net zero in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to steer the formulation of its related strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into the HKMA’s own operations and working practices. In pursuit of good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. The governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively integrated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, with effective mechanisms in place to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability efforts; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level on the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies; - in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Office; and - in other functional areas, relevant committees and working groups, which plan and implement sustainability initiatives relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability efforts across the HKMA’s different functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of ESG-related strategies, policies and plans across four functional areas: banking, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments and internal operations; - oversee the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s functional departments; - assess the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - oversee external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development matters are also invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the key outcomes of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, with a view to reinforcing Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group’s work, please refer to the chapter “Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem”.

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been working to strengthen the resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system to climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainability agenda. Banks are affected by various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by channelling capital towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risks and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”), setting out its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a sustainable finance hub in the region and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Agenda sets out eight goals in four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the goals relating to banking policy, we have been undertaking the following work. All banks strive to achieve net zero in their own operations by 2030 and in their financed emissions by 2050 All banks enhance transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2, “Transition Planning”. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks’ capacity to respond to the net-zero transition and manage the associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risks. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee’s Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosures and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on adopting the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Agenda. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address the industry’s concerns about greenwashing and help channel capital towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors and is designed to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy and the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating elements relevant to local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate green and sustainable financing. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and continued to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and address climate change. The HKMA also completed all the work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into its banking supervisory processes. To help banks enhance their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation sessions, mainly including: - establishing a robust governance framework with clearly defined responsibilities for the board and senior management - ensuring effective oversight of key areas relating to climate risks by (1) facilitating and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) maintaining appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced Supervision Roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in managing climate risks, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and financing. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA commenced a round of thematic reviews of banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management”. The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA conducted a second series of consultation sessions to assess the progress made by a new group of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, “Climate Risk Management”, and to understand the challenges they faced. The consultation sessions also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to banks’ specific circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) for the banking sector in 2024, with the participation of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results showed that the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience to severe climate-related shocks under various scenarios, including a hypothetical scenario in which climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn materialised simultaneously. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the exercise was published in February 2025. Recognising the numerous data- and methodology-related challenges banks face in managing climate risks, the HKMA has been pursuing various initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform in response to user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA has been working with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published an adoption practice guide and two Regtech Adoption Practice Guides in English, setting out technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third “FiNETech”, bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore collaboration in green fintech. Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analyses and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios to assist central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios as a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s Transition Plans Working Group, the HKMA contributed to the analysis of the interplay between the transition plans of financial and non-financial corporates and financial stability, enabling policymakers to assess climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the “Greentech Adoption Practice Guide” in English to provide financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted various applied research projects to examine the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. The research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporates’ environmental performance in cushioning monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition towards a low-carbon economy. The findings of these studies not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, supporting the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies helped strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memorandums. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlighted its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the HKIMR’s “Insights from Monetary Research” and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this participation, we help promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, while drawing insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to raising market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and facilitating more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we strive to establish Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, support technological innovation in the green finance market, enhance sustainability disclosures across the industry, expand the local green talent pool, and address knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Establishing Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures Bridging talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the Government’s commitment to tackling climate change, promoting green finance and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$28 billion equivalent to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and energy conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including their currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the Programme and further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the Programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects and it was renamed the Government Sustainable Bond Programme (the Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing institutional green bonds totalling approximately US$3 billion equivalent under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This triple-currency offering comprised RMB-, US dollar- and euro-denominated bonds of various tenors. The bonds attracted strong demand from a diverse group of investors, with subscriptions exceeding US$15 billion equivalent. The 20- and 30-year RMB green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and were its longest-tenor RMB bonds to date, providing new benchmarks for the market and further demonstrating the role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the range of offshore RMB investment products available in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuance reflected their recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to raise funds for sustainable development through Hong Kong’s financing platform, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, providing grants for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry. As at the end of 2024, grants had been approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion. In May 2024, the Scheme was extended for three years to 2027, with its scope expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The extension and expansion of the Scheme aim to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to use Hong Kong’s transition financing platform to progressively decarbonise. - Grants approved for around 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion (as at the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope expanded to cover transition finance instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, achieving encouraging results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB7 billion, including RMB2.7 billion of green bonds, RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds and RMB0.9 billion of social bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion of green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, including RMB1 billion of blue bonds and RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds. These bond issuances once again underscored Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. With the above measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred sustainable financing platform in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong remained the largest arranging hub for international green and sustainable bond issuances in Asia in 2024, with bonds arranged in Hong Kong totalling US$43.1 billion and accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world’s first tokenised government green bond and the world’s first multi-currency digital bond respectively. These issuances demonstrated the Government’s support for regional market participants in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in green and sustainable finance. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working towards the adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosures, making such disclosures more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (Questionnaire), launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to enable businesses to complete it online (see the QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, including by identifying core questions and providing common use cases for the Questionnaire. In addition, we are seeking to enhance the Questionnaire’s compatibility with other supporting tools on the Steering Group’s website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, thereby demonstrating its commitment. The Report contains extensive information on the HKMA’s climate-related operational risks, as well as its plans and implementation progress towards achieving its climate targets. For details of sustainability disclosures relating to our own operations, please refer to the “Sustainable HKMA” chapter. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training for the banking industry and facilitating knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to bridge knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local banking practitioners’ knowledge and skills in sustainable finance, the HKMA and the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB) launched the Core Level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework in July 2023. The module aims to help banking professionals acquire knowledge and develop professional capabilities in green and sustainable finance more effectively, and covers four major areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance and governance. In addition, the Professional Level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module, targeting middle- and senior-level banking practitioners responsible for related work, was launched in November. To provide banking practitioners with the necessary training, the HKIB, as the administrator of the Green and Sustainable Finance module, launched the training programme for its Core Level in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking industry in 2025 to develop a training programme for the Professional Level. To understand the banking industry’s further skills and training needs, the HKMA is currently working with the industry on the “Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026–2030” study, with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study follows up on the “Capacity Building for Future Banking 2021–2025” paper published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry in formulating and adjusting talent development strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through its collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continued to support the implementation of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students undertaking sustainability-related training. As at December 2024, 85 international and local programmes had been registered as eligible training programmes under the Scheme, and more than 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025–26 Budget that the Scheme would be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to facilitate skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in establishing a chapter in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can go hand in hand, the HKMA adheres to the principle of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritises sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of “capital preservation first, long-term growth thereafter”, the HKMA believes that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate the associated investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the urgent issue of climate change, with a view to enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We incorporate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner and continuously explore a range of investment vehicles to channel capital towards sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the “HKMA ESG Expectations” and made the document available to investment partners through its annual ESG Workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we strive to foster a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the Exchange Fund’s investments. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to pursue responsible investment while fulfilling the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees the ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Sub-Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Proposals and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across the HKMA’s different functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate, across different investments: - Public market investments — The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolios through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Division. The Sustainable Investment Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (see “Promoting active ownership” under the “Risk Management” section on page 39 for details). - Private market investments — The Investment Sub-Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal conducted by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks arising from climate change, as well as the related opportunities, could affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2024 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that average global temperatures will rise by 2.6°C to 3.1°C above pre-industrial levels unless there is large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Uncertainty surrounding policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may intensify transition risks, leading to greater market volatility and affecting asset valuations. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also expose investments to additional risks of physical damage and financial loss. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates investment opportunities with potentially attractive long-term prospects in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related considerations when integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set a target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and continues to make progress towards this target through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the “Action Agenda”, which reinforced the Exchange Fund’s commitments and efforts relating to the climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement over excluding or divesting from investments. Investing in a sustainable future Achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier - Actively expanding the scope and range of sustainable investments, particularly investments focused on climate transition themes in the public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition pathway considerations - Establishing clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to follow them - Committing to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolios by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030 or earlier Supporting the region’s transition through investment - Continuing to engage with external investment managers to enhance investment opportunities that advance the transition - Continuing to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia’s transition and deliver positive global impact First, maintaining diversified and robust portfolios is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investible universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. By adopting an inclusive approach, the HKMA can capture opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition and equipped with superior technologies and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core “brown” industries. Merely excluding or divesting from such investments would not help address carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by providing strategic capital and exercising active ownership, encouraging them to transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices and thereby effecting positive change both within the industries themselves and globally. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition pathways, with a view to driving economy-wide decarbonisation. As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognises that the long-term resilience of its portfolios depends not only on the alignment of the portfolios themselves, but also on a broad-based economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy in 2024 by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to driving the transition while supporting the net-zero objectives of both the Exchange Fund and the world. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including ESG integration and stewardship in fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting a range of assets aligned with pathways towards net-zero emissions. In the public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or providers of climate solutions, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In the private markets, greater emphasis may be placed on investments that facilitate the transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate the climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolios. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for more than 10% of the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio”, with financial performance comparable to the benchmarks of the relevant portfolios (Figure 5). - Public market investments — The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focusing on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the use of a customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continued to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that finance sustainable projects while offering competitive returns (see “Enhancing sustainability through GSS bonds” for related case studies). - Private market investments — The HKMA is committed to building resilient portfolios for long-term growth by capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and evaluates investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see “Joining forces to address climate challenges in Asia and globally” for examples). - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios not benchmarked against ESG indices - Actively managed governance-themed portfolios - Actively managed ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonisation globally, in Asia and in the Global South - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation and focused on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The “MCPP One Planet” programme, which provides Paris-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-government institution. The proceeds of the green bond were allocated to various projects, including upgrades to ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades covered enhancements to monitoring and control systems and pump performance, generating positive environmental benefits through wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling. In addition to the ongoing treatment of wastewater and sludge, the facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recycling rate of up to 100%. The facilities also use gas generated during sludge treatment to fuel boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond financed various projects, including the rehabilitation of a country’s canal system. As one of the country’s largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess river flows to arid areas. The project’s primary objective is to rehabilitate the deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project provided skills training to local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA’s key priorities in delivering on this commitment in 2024 was its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target and in line with the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda”. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is committed to fostering staff development and well-being, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee) is the principal decision-making body for corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to climate action, the Steering Committee endorsed in October 2024 the HKMA’s new target of achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by or before 2030 as part of the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) provides guidance on implementing sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. The Green Office Task Force and Volunteer Team, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ways to create a greener workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” Logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around the three pillars of Environment, People and Social Responsibility. - Focus on decarbonising and digitalising the HKMA’s daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2030 - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with Government guidelines - Promote greener practices within the financial sector and the wider community - Build an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring and inclusive workplace that values diversity and strengthens staff’s sense of belonging - Provide a quality work environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Foster a caring culture - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education initiatives The HKMA takes climate change seriously and leads by example. In October 2024, as part of the “Action Agenda”, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment. The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the transition towards net zero, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations by reducing carbon emissions, conserving energy and paper, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for power generation by local electricity companies. In addition, the HKMA has established a digital workplace to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. The HKMA also recognises the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overriding 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procure low-carbon products and services wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023 the HKMA has fully offset carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offsetting programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market’s low-carbon transition through measures ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to the promotion of electronic payments and the collection of coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter sets out in detail the HKMA’s strategies for environmental stewardship, promoting staff well-being and caring for the community. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing and reviewing the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To assess more effectively the possible operational impacts of climate change, the HKMA identifies various climate-related risks and reviews their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring operational continuity, the design of the HKMA’s offices incorporates various measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption and paper usage arising from its own operations. The HKMA’s latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with its corporate operations by or before 2030. These targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology. The HKMA adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s major greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In the absence of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimating major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods, including capital goods, and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” appended to the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example and adheres to the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green transportation, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 with a view to achieving fully green transportation. The HKMA continues to incorporate environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects undertaken in 2024, the HKMA reduced waste by reusing existing furniture and fitting-out materials or trading in old items for new ones. To improve overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in its offices and data centres.
