As part of a data centre facility upgrade project in 2024, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows flexible capacity expansion, enhances operational efficiency at partial loads, and incorporates advanced cooling technologies and higher power density, thereby helping reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace and streamlines workflows, effectively reducing paper usage. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers’ software update cycles, thereby prolonging the period during which the devices can be used securely. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the “4R” principles of refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and regularly conducts waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are placed at convenient locations throughout the HKMA’s offices. To increase recycling rates, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit nets in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Pledge for Events”, committing to take measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications in the Government’s “Green Procurement List”, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, such as by consolidating multiple trips wherever possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in Gold Standard-certified carbon offsetting programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these programmes focus on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” from Earth Day on 22 April 2024 throughout May under the theme “Think Green, Live Green, Work Green”. This provided a valuable opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to and momentum in putting environmental sustainability into practice in its internal operations. The programme included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to practise green living, a “Save the Earth” quiz, and a workshop on caring for “kokedama” indoor plants originating from Japan. The results of the waste audit were also shared, and an operator of a community recycling centre introduced recycling best practices. To sustain the momentum of “Green Month”, the HKMA launched a recycling campaign lasting approximately six months in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that the collective impact of small changes in individual habits could significantly improve the organisation’s overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of the “Green ‘Fit’ Action” video, in which senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders to encourage staff to take action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their awareness of sustainability and collect their views on proposed green office measures. The survey findings will help shape future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as an important agent of change and is therefore committed to leading and accelerating the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable practices within the financial sector and the wider community. The HKMA has introduced various measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the Common Data Submission Platform in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform’s coverage in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, facilitating their submission of certain regulatory information. The expanded coverage aims to further streamline the submission processes of reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives introduced in 2024 included SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys through a streamlined submission process, and the Smart Information and Document Management System, a centralised platform that provides users with advanced search capabilities for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the “Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the “HKMA”). The Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from air travel for 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data include Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, as well as their corresponding intensities. The HKMA’s GHG emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the “GHG Protocol”), jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered a total of six office and warehouse premises, comprising five offices located at (1) Two International Finance Centre, (2) Hopewell Centre, (3) One Pacific Place, (4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and (5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at (6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the six premises. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion at a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The completeness and accuracy of the Data were tested by tracing selected sample data back to their sources. The underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking were also reviewed and tested for reliability. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the Data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance over the Data and concludes that: - the Data are materially accurate and reliable; and - the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Siu Yan Shum Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
